strings.name: Othman Benjelloun
strings.role: Chairman and CEO of Bank of Africa; Chairman of O Capital Group
strings.summary: Othman Benjelloun is a Moroccan financial executive who has led BMCE since its privatization in 1995. During his leadership, the bank expanded its African business by investing in and then taking control of the BOA network, later adopting the Bank of Africa name. He also founded the BMCE Bank Foundation to support rural education and environmental protection.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Bank founding, privatization, equity investment and renaming are distinguished; corporate stakes are not personal holdings, and establishing educational projects does not prove their social impact.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed Moroccan banking and insurance businesses, advancing cross-border financial networks and industrial investment in Africa.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and education
strings.facts.f1.value: The bank’s annual report records his birth in Casablanca in 1932. Bank and holding-company biographies describe him as a Lausanne polytechnic graduate without giving a graduation year.
strings.facts.f2.label: Bank history
strings.facts.f2.value: BMCE was founded in 1959 and privatized in 1995. His board service began in 1995, which must not be described as the bank’s founding year.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Expanding an African banking network
strings.highlights.h1.text: Under his leadership, BMCE acquired 35% of BOA Group in 2008 and increased its stake to 55.77% in 2010, moving from minority investment to control.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Supporting rural education
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded the BMCE Bank Foundation in 1995; its subsequent Medersat.com program developed rural schools alongside an environmental mission.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Attends Mohammed VI Tower inauguration
strings.timeline.t1.text: Reports named him among those welcoming the Crown Prince; the tower project was promoted by O Capital Group, which he chairs.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Bank adopts a new name
strings.timeline.t2.text: BMCE BANK OF AFRICA became BANK OF AFRICA–BMCE Group.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Name highlights African business
strings.timeline.t3.text: The bank adopted the BMCE BANK OF AFRICA name to reflect its African business orientation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Acquires majority control of BOA
strings.timeline.t4.text: BMCE’s stake in BOA Group reached 55.77%, an investment by the bank.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Completes initial BOA investment
strings.timeline.t5.text: A BOA Group capital increase was completed, giving BMCE a 35% stake.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First rural schools open
strings.timeline.t6.text: The BMCE Bank Foundation’s Medersat.com program opened its first rural schools.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Medersat.com program launches
strings.timeline.t7.text: The foundation launched its rural education program; at a September forum that year, he reaffirmed its education and environmental commitments.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Leads privatized BMCE
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began serving on the bank’s board and leading the bank; founded the BMCE Bank Foundation that same year.
